heroHeadline: 30,000 Displaced by Cité Soleil Violence Wave; MSF Hospital Day 12 Closed; WFP Reaches 8,500 With Emergency Food; Shalom Church Shelters 2,000+
heroSubtitle: UN News (May 20) confirmed approximately 30,000 people have been displaced since gang fighting erupted on May 10 in Cité Soleil and the Cul-de-Sac Plain, with the Shalom Church in Delmas 33 sheltering over 2,000 displaced persons and WFP reaching 8,500 newly displaced with emergency food assistance (rice, pulses, oil, fortified flour). Nine WFP-supported schools serving some 12,000 students suspended meal distributions. On May 21, Africanews documented gangs continuing to burn houses and vehicles across Ouest and Artibonite departments as the displacement surge entered its second week. MSF's Cité Soleil hospital — the only emergency medical facility for the commune's ~300,000 residents — entered Day 12 of closure on May 21, with no announced reopening timeline as gang conditions remain unmet for safe access. The GSF's ~800-person advance force under Mongolian Maj. Gen. Erdenebat Batsuuri (commanding since May 14) remains entirely concentrated in Port-au-Prince's city center, leaving Cité Soleil, the Cul-de-Sac corridor, and all of the Artibonite without international security coverage. PM Fils-Aimé's May 12 declaration that August 30 elections are 'impossible' stands unrevised; no electoral decree issued; voter registration has not begun; 23 communes remain inaccessible. Approximately 350,000 Haitian TPS holders in the US await the Supreme Court's ruling on Noem v. Doe / Trump v. Miot — expected late June 2026. Total displacement now estimated at ~1.5 million; 6.4 million in acute food insecurity; the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan is only ~20% funded ($172M of $880M needed).
